text:
kevin: Quick sync — proposing a rollout plan for FlashAttention v3 kernels. We want safe canary + staged ramp, plus fallback to v2/fused when we see regressions. High level: feature flag, kernel chooser update, canary nodes, perf/QA gating, KV-cache validation.

maria: +1. main concerns: KV cache correctness for paged attention transitions and memory profiler skewing with v3 kernels.

sara: Do we have a concrete kernel selection heuristic yet? seq_len / attention type / quantization all matter.

kevin: Draft chooser logic i used in local tests:
```python
# kernel chooser pseudocode
if model.supports_flashv3 and seq_len <= 2048 and not quantized_int8:
    kernel = "flash_v3"
elif model.supports_paged_attention and seq_len > 2048:
    kernel = "paged_attention"
else:
    kernel = "fused_attention"
```
Notes: we avoid flash_v3 for int8 quantized weights until we validate numeric parity. Also prefer paged for long sequences to keep memory stable.

jeff: We should gate flash_v3 behind two flags: a global on/off + canary set. Example:
```yaml
feature_flags:
  flashattn_v3: off
  flashattn_v3_canary: ["canary-1","canary-2","team-language"]
```
Canary should be both node-based and tenant-based.

maria: I ran a small profile on the Llama-13B-ish workload. synthetic perf (single request):
```
before (fused): p95 18.2ms, p50 9.7ms, mem 6.8GB
flash_v2: p95 15.6ms, p50 8.9ms, mem 6.1GB
flash_v3 (local): p95 12.9ms, p50 7.1ms, mem 5.9GB
```
BUT noticed higher allocation churn in the runtime allocator (peak RSS similar though). Need to check our allocator hooks and KV cache warm path.

kevin: Good data. For the KV cache: ensure page-aligned allocations and that we don't reorder cache entries when switching kernels. If we change KV layout between v2 and v3, we must invalidate or provide compatibility layer.

sara: Agreed. We should add a compatibility bit to the model metadata: `kv_layout_version`. If layout differs, force KV cache miss + refill. Simple approach for rollout.

jeff: Rollout plan proposal (short):
- Feature flag default off.
- Canary 1: internal infra & perf teams only (2 nodes). bake 48h, run perf harness.
- Canary 2: small customer subset (team-language + 3 small tenants). bake 72h. monitor regressions.
- Ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over weeks with automatic rollback on regression thresholds.
- Metrics: p95 latency, error rate, model output diff rate (eval prompts), KV cache miss rate, OOM events.

maria: Perf regression thresholds: p95 increase >5% OR output-drift >1% on eval set -> auto rollback. Also OOM or CPU spike >20% -> immediate rollback.

perf-bot: Automated check: run diff eval daily on canaries. Uploading initial run: https://perf.example.com/run/3582 (summaries attached) :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: `rbox deploy --image runtime:feat/flashv3 --canary canary-1,canary-2 --flags flashattn_v3_canary`

jeff: For kernel chooser, add a small probed path: first request on a node can try flash_v3 in a safe sandboxed trace mode (no output to customer) to detect correctness and latency. If trace shows mismatch, mark node as tainted and fall back.

maria: On KV behavior: I'm going to run an end-to-end test that does mixed seq_len workloads to ensure we don't leak stale KV pointers. Will post logs.

kevin: Action items: @maria run KV mixed workload (due EOD), @sara add kv_layout_version field + chooser changes (PR draft), @jeff implement flag gating + rollout automation, perf-bot to upload baseline diffs.

sara: I'll open PR with chooser + feature flag wiring. planning to include a `--trace-sandbox` opt per node.

jeff: I'll coordinate canary nodes and add rollback playbook to runbook (include steps to force v2 kernel via env var).

maria: Quick FYI: saw a weird regression on a 32k seq test with flash_v3 — p95 spiked to 2.1x but it was because the runtime fell back to fallback fused kernel mid-request due to a page fault and reallocation. Investigating.

kevin: Thanks — that's exactly why we need the canaries. Keep notes here and link logs. If anyone sees output-drift >0.5% ping me immediately.

jeff: thumbs up. I'll kick off the canary deploy now.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started at 1759001900 on canary-1, canary-2. Monitor: https://rbox.monitor/canaries/flashv3

perf-bot: First 1h canary summary: p95 -12% vs baseline, p50 -22%, no OOMs, output-diff 0.13%. Continuing monitoring. :rocket:
